sentences.text: Gilchristosuchus is an extinct genus of neosuchian crocodyliform named after the ranch owners where the type specimen was discovered.
The type species is Gilchristosuchus palatinus, named for its distinctive palatine bones.
The skull of Gilchristosuchus would have been approximately 15 cm long when complete.
Fossils of Gilchristosuchus were found in the upper Milk River Formation of Alberta, Canada, dating to the Late Cretaceous.
The genus Gilchristosuchus was described in 1993 by scientists Wu and Brinkman.
Despite its small size, the skull ornamentation and bone fusion indicate that the specimen was an adult.
Gilchristosuchus belongs to the parent group Neosuchia.
Gilchristosuchus is classified within the class Reptilia.
Gilchristosuchus lived during the Santonian stage, between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago.
Researchers suggested that Gilchristosuchus was the most derived neosuchian crocodyliform that did not belong to Eusuchia, the group containing all living crocodilians.
